content: To help manage or prevent certain diseases, it is essential to adopt specific lifestyle changes. These include reducing stress levels, consuming a diet low in fat and salt, losing weight if you are overweight, engaging in regular physical activity, and quitting smoking. To support cognitive health and reduce the risk of dementia, keep your mind active by participating in mental exercises such as reading or solving crossword puzzles. For maintaining healthy bones, lifestyle modifications should include increasing weight-bearing exercises, avoiding smoking, limiting alcohol consumption, and eating a well-balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D. If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store your medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about the product and your specific health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, or weight changes. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. In rare cases, this medication may cause serious, potentially fatal complications such as blood clots, including heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs. Severe allergic reactions to this product are also rare. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid smoking or using tobacco products. Inform your doctor if you have recently undergone or will undergo surgery, or if you will be confined to a chair or bed for an extended period (e.g., during a long plane flight), as these conditions increase the risk of blood clots, especially if you are taking an estrogen product. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on your face and skin (melasma). Sunlight can worsen this effect, so limit your time in the sun and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, which could potentially affect their growth and development. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It can pass into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., metyrapone test), potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, regular complete physical exams, including laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., blood pressure, breast exam/mammogram, pelvic exam, Pap smear), should be conducted. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Preventing or managing high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes can significantly reduce your risk of heart disease and stroke. Lifestyle changes that can help control or prevent these conditions include reducing stress, eating a low-fat and low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking. To maintain cognitive health, engage in activities that stimulate your mind, such as reading or solving puzzles. To promote healthy bones, incorporate weight-bearing exercises, avoid smoking, limit alcohol intake, and consume a balanced diet with sufficient calcium and vitamin D.
